reason: The text explicitly demonstrates the opposite of antagonism. The Israelites follow Moses's instructions precisely ('וּבְנֵי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל עָשׂ֖וּ כִּדְבַ֣ר מֹשֶׁ֑ה' - 'the children of Israel did according to the word of Moses'). Moses is described as 'גָּדוֹל מְאֹד' (great greatly) in the eyes of both Pharaoh's servants and the people, indicating respect and positive regard. The people obey Moses's commands regarding the spoils from Egypt and the preparation of unleavened bread without complaint or resistance. There is no indication of antagonism toward Moses's leadership; rather, the narrative shows complete compliance and deference.
